chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Mismāʿ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was presented with a man who had killed a pig, so he held him liable for compensation; and a man was presented to him who had broken a barbat, so he nullified it.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْإِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the report
key_terms.خِنْزِيرًا: a pig, mentioned here as the subject of legal compensation
key_terms.فَأَبْطَلَهُ: he invalidated it or annulled liability regarding it
key_terms.فَضَمَّنَهُ: he made him liable for compensation
key_terms.مِسْمَعٍ: Mismāʿ, a narrator in the sanad

ai.seo_question: What did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام rule about killing a pig and breaking a barbat?
ai.summary: This hadith reports two legal judgments of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning damage to property. In one case, compensation was imposed for killing a pig, while in the other, liability was invalidated for breaking a barbat, reflecting distinctions in legal value and compensability.
